title: Prisma Client Queries Overview
description: Learn how Prisma Client executes queries, understands method semantics, and optimizes queries via its Rust engine.

data.text: Prisma Client provides an intuitive, promise-based API for interacting with your database. Every model defined in your `schema.prisma` exposes a dedicated model delegate (e.g. `prisma.user`, `prisma.order`) containing specialized methods for reading, inserting, updating, and deleting records.

data.text: A common question in database interviews is why Prisma differentiates `findUnique` from `findFirst`. `findUnique` enforces at compile-time that you query by an indexed unique field (e.g. `id`, `email`, or a composite `@@unique`). This guarantees that PostgreSQL performs an index lookup with `O(log N)` complexity. In contrast, `findFirst` allows non-unique filters which might result in sequential table scans if not indexed properly.

data.title: Use `findUniqueOrThrow` for Route Handlers
data.text: When building Next.js dynamic routes (e.g. `/api/users/[id]`), `findUniqueOrThrow()` automatically throws a `PrismaClientKnownRequestError` with code `P2025` if the entity is missing, allowing centralized error handling to return an HTTP 404 response.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `findUnique` whenever querying by primary key or unique fields.
Use `findFirst` when filtering by non-unique fields or ordering by date.
`findMany` returns an empty array `[]` when no rows match, while `findUnique` and `findFirst` return `null`.
